title: Ruling 2022-03: Exemption for Purchase of Building Materials to Construct or Alter Building Owned by Local Development Corporation
text:
Date: Not provided

Written by: Emily Bergquist

Approved by Craig Bolio, Commissioner of Taxes

This is a formal ruling for your client, [taxpayer], regarding the applicability of sales and use tax to purchases of building materials and supplies to be used in the acquisition and conversion of a former warehouse. This ruling is based upon representations in your letter dated [date], received in this office [date].

Facts 

The facts as you described them are as follows:

1. Your client, [Taxpayer] (Taxpayer), is a Vermont limited partnership.

2. [Corporation] is a Vermont nonprofit corporation, an exempt entity under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (IRC), and a "local development corporation" as defined in 10 V.S.A. § 212(10)3. Taxpayer and [Corporation] will enter into a project to acquire the [location] in [town], a former [business type] warehouse, and then convert the building for mixed use with commercial tenants, including [tenant], and rental housing units.

3. Taxpayer and [Corporation] will enter into a project toc acquire the [location] in [town], a former [business type] warehouse, and then convert the building for mixed use with commercial tenants, including [tenant], and rental housing units.

4. [Corporation] will receive grants from [Commission], [Commission], [Board], and the [Town]. [Corporation] will receive a [Credit] awarded through the [Board] in accordance with 32 V.SA. §§ 5930aa - 5930ff.

5. [Corporation] "will acquire the fee interest" in the [location]. It is presumed for the purpose of this ruling that you use the quoted phrase to mean that [Corporation] will own the building.

Due to requirements under Federal income tax law in IRC §§ 42 and 47, governing Rehabilitation Tax Credits and Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, Taxpayer and [Corporation] intend to have [Corporation] lease the [location] to Taxpayer for a term of 99 years. [Corporation] will lend to Taxpayer funds from [Corporations]'s [Credit] award. Taxpayer will use these funds, plus capital contributions from its general and limited partners, plus proceeds from private loans, to pay for rehabilitation of the [location], including purchase of building

materials and supplies to be incorporated into the building.

7. You have asked whether Taxpayer's purchases of materials and supplies for use in the conversion of the [location] will be exempt from sales tax under 32 V.S.A. § 9743(4).

Discussion 

Vermont sales and use tax does not apply to the following:

(4) Sales of building materials and supplies to be used in the construction, reconstruction, alteration, remodeling, or repair of . . .

(C) any building or structure owned by any "local development corporation" as defined in 10 V.S.A. § 212(10), and used exclusively for the

purposes authorized in 10 V.S.A. Chapter 12; provided, however, that the . . . development corporation has first obtained a certificate from the Commissioner stating that it is entitled to the exemption and the vendor keeps a record of the sales price of each separate sale, the name of the purchaser, the date of each separate sale, and the number of the certificate.

32 V.S.A. § 9743(4). For an eligible project, this exemption covers purchases of the following:

In this subdivision, the words "building materials and supplies" shall include all materials and supplies consumed, employed, or expended in the construction, reconstruction, alteration, remodeling, or repair of any building, structure, or other public work as well as the materials and supplies physically incorporated therein.

32 V.S.A. § 9743(4)(C).

Under Subsection (C) of Subsection 9743(4), quoted above, the sales tax exemption applies only to materials and supplies used in altering a building owned by a "local development corporation" as defined in Title 10 and "used exclusively for the purposes authorized in Chapter 12 of Title 10." In addition, the exemption is available only if the local development corporation first obtains exemption certification from the Commissioner of Taxes, and only if each vendor of the materials and supplies keeps records of each sale as required by Subdivision (C).

In Taxpayer's case, the ruling request letter states that the building to be altered will be owned by [Corporation] and that [Corporation] is a "local Development corporation" as defined in Title 10. Thus, the first requirement for the sales tax exemption is met.

The [location] will, however, not be "used exclusively for the purposes authorized in chapter 12 of Title 10." The relevant "purposes authorized in Chapter 12" of Title 10 are found in Sections 210 and 212 of thx chapter. Section 210 states:

§ 210. Statutory purposes 

The statutory purpose of the exemption for local development corporations in Section 236 of this title is to promote economic development. 10 V.S.A. § 210. This broad statement of purpose is narrowed by the definition of "eligible project" in Section 212:

(6) "Eligible facility" or "eligible project" means any industrial, commercial, or agricultural enterprise or endeavor approved by the Authority that meets the criteria established in the Vermont Sustainable Jobs Strategy adopted by the Governor under section 280b of this title, including land and rights in land, air, or water, buildings, structures, machinery, and equipment of such eligible facilities or eligible projects, except that an eligible facility or project shall not include the portion of an enterprise or endeavor relating to the sale of goods at retail where such goods are manufactured primarily out of state, and except further that an eligible facility or project shall not include the portion of an enterprise or endeavor relating to housing. 

10 V.S.A. § 212(6).

Since the [location] will be altered for commercial tenants, but also to provide rental housing units, the building will not be "used exclusively for the purposes authorized in chapter 12 of Title 10." The portion of the [location] used for housing will not meet the second requirement for the sales tax exemption and thus will not be eligible for the exemption.

It is not stated whether any commercial tenant of the [location] will sell "at retail . . . goods . . . manufactured primarily out of state." Any portion of the building to be used for retail of such goods would also not be eligible for the sales tax exemption.

As noted earlier, the sales tax exemption only applies to purchases made after the local development corporation "has first obtained a certificate from the Commissioner stating that it is entitled to the exemption." Taxpayer may obtain the Commissioner's certification by request from the Taxpayer Services Division at the Department. Taxpayer may then complete Form S-3C, which is the exemption certificate for "Contractors Completing a Qualified Exempt Project." Taxpayer must present the completed Form S-3C to its sellers at the time it purchases the building materials and supplies for the eligible portion of this project.

General Provisions 

Issuance of this ruling is conditioned upon the understanding that neither the taxpayer nor a related taxpayer is currently under audit or involved in an administrative appeal or litigation concerning the subject matters of the ruling. This ruling is issued solely to the taxpayer and is limited to the facts presented, as affected by current statutes and regulations.

Other taxpayers may refer to this ruling, when redacted to protect confidentiality, to see the Department's general approach, but the Department will not be bound by this ruling in the case of any other taxpayer or in the case of any change in the relevant statutes or regulations.

This ruling will be made public after deletion of the taxpayer's name and any information which may identify the taxpayer. A copy of this ruling showing the proposed deletions is attached, and you may request within 30 days that the Commissioner delete any further information that might identify the taxpayer. The final discretion as to deletions rests with the Commissioner.

You have the right to appeal this rulingwithin 30 days.. 3 V.S.A. §§ 808, B15.
